args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to us-east, us-west, eu-west) was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and why an unhealthy release candidate got promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** Every region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) was running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rolling back to a version that was already healthy didn't need change-manager approval. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the result. There were no open incidents before it.

The test version of v2.3.1 was also failing in staging, but it still went to production. The incident lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 fails, and why a version that failed in staging was released.
